findings.body: If committed AGENTS.md links to CLAUDE.md, deleting CLAUDE.md leaves AGENTS.md dangling and removes the instructions from the checkout. This is reachable in forge-source, where `_held` ignores committed history. When the linked text already matches sync, AGENTS.md is skipped entirely; otherwise its write goes through the link before the target is deleted. Doctor can also commit this broken link in its default-branch fix. `sync.write` prevents this by materializing instruction-file links first (src/forge/sync.py:335-345). Preserve their contents as regular files before removing CLAUDE.md, and cover this through doctor’s real command.

findings.body: After doctor repairs both hosts’ files in place, they match sync but remain unstaged, as required. On the next run, this set includes those unstaged modifications and sends matching files to `_held`, producing hand-edit rows and exit status 1 for doctor’s own repairs. `repo.git` trims leading whitespace (src/forge/repo.py:82), accidentally misparsing the first status entry, but the second repaired file reliably triggers this defect. New evidence relative to the previous staged-edit finding is a repeated successful in-place repair with no staged or manual changes. Force-check matching files only for staged differences, and parse untrimmed status output.
findings.title: Not done: Doctor never overwrites a change made by hand, and leaves what needs a person as one plain step

findings.body: A clean, tracked empty CLAUDE.md is skipped because its text equals the wanted empty string. However, empty wanted text means deletion: githooks supplies this entry whenever CLAUDE.md exists (src/forge/githooks.py:74), and sync explicitly counts an existing empty file as a change (src/forge/sync.py:347-349). Consequently doctor neither removes it in place nor includes its removal in a default-branch fix, and reports no drift. Include physical existence when detecting deletion targets and cover an empty file in both repair paths.
